To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

thin superconductor - normal metal bilayer has unique superconductiv properties, which are determined by the ratio of resistivities $\rho_S/\rho_N$ of superconductor and normal metal layers, and may be used in construction of superconducting devices.
thin dirty superconducting-normal metal bilayer has a unique superconducting behavior due to the presence of the large resistivity contrast.
thin dirty superconducting-normal metal bilayer has unique superconductivity properties which are not observed in single superconductors and which can be used in superconducting detectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of a superconductor-normal-metal bilayer system.

the study of superconducting thin film of a dirty material in parallel magnetic field $H$. The main attention is paid to the case where the normal state resistivity of the film is much larger than the normal state resistive of the superconductor.
the study of the superconducting properties and critical current of thin dirty superconductive-normal metal bilayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the superconducting properties in the thin superconductor - normal metal bilayer with the large resistivity ratio of $\rho_N/\rho_S$ are quite different from the ones in the superconductor - superconductor bilayer.
the normal layer in the bilayer structure is the key factor for the enhancement of superconducting response of whole system.
the superconducting properties and the superconductor-normal layer interface are very important in the superconducting bilayer structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the superconductor-normal bilayer with small resistivity of the normal layer is a good candidate for a new kind of superconducting detector.
the normal metal layer may be considered as a new tool in design of superconducting devices.

the presence of the thin normal layer in superconductor-normal-metal bilayer with $\rho_N\ll \rho_S$ leads to a number of peculiarities in its superconducting properties which are absent in the case of $\rho_N\gg \rho_S$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the normal layer may play a role of a filter for the superconducting layer, providing its protection from external perturbation.
the presence of the thin normal layer in superconducting device may lead to the enhancement of its performance in wide interval of temperatures and magnetic fields.
the superconducting properties can be significantly improved if we add to the superconductor a thin film of a material with a much higher resistivity.
